verdict_reasoning: The problem is stated and demand is shown, and no surviving objection is fatal. Level 2 is not yet settled. replication-ondisk-1 (in-place batch checksums under share-locked hint-bit updates) and replication-ondisk-2 (the recovery assert failure and untraced invalid-page warnings) are open safety points. standards-compat-1 and standards-compat-2 change the measured behaviour of checkpoint_completion_target and bgwriter_lru_maxpages. All are fixable inside this design, and they need someone who knows the buffer manager and recovery.

brief.title: Write combining for checkpointer, bgwriter, backends and bulkwrite
brief.problem: Postgres writes dirty shared buffers one block at a time, so checkpoints and buffer cleaning use many small write IOs. This limits write throughput, most of all on IOPS-limited storage. The author also says all writers will need write combining before Postgres can use direct IO.
brief.proposed_design: The checkpointer, bgwriter, client backends and the bulkwrite strategy ring write runs of contiguous dirty blocks as one vectored write of up to io_combine_limit. Backends and bgwriter look for dirty blocks before and after the victim block. The series also refactors victim buffer selection and adds a WriteBuffersOperation object shaped for later AIO writes.
user_visible_surface: dtrace probe buffer__sync__written renamed to buffers__sync__written; it now reports buffers per combined IO, not a buffer ID.
pg_stat_io: evictions and reuses counted once when invalidating a victim buffer fails; backends and bgwriter now show larger writes.
io_combine_limit now also caps write size, not only read size.
test_aio module gains functions to dirty, flush and invalidate specific relation blocks.
author_claims: Immediate checkpoints are at least 20% faster (about 6.5 s to 5 s, 16 GiB shared_buffers, local SSD).
pgbench scale 500 on IOPS-limited storage: about 30% more TPS and 75% better p99 latency; almost 70% more TPS with synchronous_commit off.
Most of the gain comes from client backends combining their own writes; checkpointer combining adds little there because the kernel already combines its writes.
The API shape will carry over to AIO writes with separate start, completion and wait phases.
brief.thread_state: Andrey Borodin, Chao Li, Haibo Yan and shihao zhong have reviewed v16; open items include spread checkpoints finishing early, bgwriter_lru_maxpages being exceeded, and an assert failure during recovery from a base backup. The checksum race with hint bits waits on separate work by Andres, and the author reported an intermittent invalid-page warning in v14.
unclear: No v16 benchmark results for spread checkpoints, which reviewers say now finish much too early.
The material does not say whether the checksum-on-shared-lock race is fixed in v16 or still waits for the hint-bit lock work.
No answer yet on how neighbors should count against bgwriter_lru_maxpages.
The material does not say whether the intermittent invalid-page warning from v14 was found and fixed.
Vacuum and bulkread write combining are not enabled or benchmarked.

prior_attempts.title: Vectored I/O in bulk_write.c
prior_attempts.quote: I'd like to try something more ambitious that streamifies this and also the "main" writeback paths.
prior_attempts.reason: The author decided not to commit it for v17. He chose to try a broader design that would use streaming writes for this path and for the main writeback paths. Andres Freund's objection to merging smgrzeroextend() into the same interface was settled by dropping that part, so it did not decide the outcome. Noah Misch later asked whether the CF entry was obsolete, and the visible messages show no reply.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P2 combined writes only in bulk_write.c, and its author set it aside to try a broader design that also covers the main writeback paths. This proposal covers those paths (checkpointer, bgwriter, backends, bulkwrite ring), with synchronous writes and without streams.

objections.title: Batch checksum on shared lock can write pages with stale checksums
objections.failure_scenario: On a cluster with data checksums, a query sets a hint bit under a share lock while a combined write holds the batch. The page reaches disk with a checksum computed before the hint change. A later read, pg_basebackup verification or a standby reports a checksum failure on a page that is not corrupt.
objections.argument: Message #24 says the batch path checksums pages in place, unlike master's PageSetChecksumCopy(), and calls the series uncommittable until separate hint-bit lock work lands. The material does not show that the v16 write path has removed this dependency. Every combined write in checkpointer, bgwriter and backends would then depend on work outside this proposal.
objections.author_must_show: Does v16 copy pages before checksumming them, and if not, which committed lock change makes in-place batch checksums safe under share-locked hint-bit updates?

critic.reasoning: Message #24 says in-place batch checksums are not committable until the hint-bit lock work lands. Nothing in the visible v16 prose says that the dependency is met or that pages are copied before checksumming.

objections.title: WAL-before-data rule for combined writes during recovery is not stated
objections.failure_scenario: A user restores a base backup and starts recovery with checksums off. The startup process writes a combined batch whose neighbor LSN is past what XLogFlush() can satisfy. An assert build crashes, and a production build writes the batch with only a warning, so nothing checks the rule there.
objections.argument: Message #43 shows the new WriteBuffers() assert failing in recovery, because XLogFlush() only updates minRecoveryPoint and warns there. Message #40 confirms that neighbors can raise max_lsn above what the required victim needs. Messages #27 and #30 report intermittent invalid-page errors in 027_stream_regress and a zeroed FSM page with no root cause found. The proposal does not state which invariant a combined write keeps on a standby, during crash recovery and at a restartpoint.
objections.author_must_show: What rule ties a combined batch's max_lsn to minRecoveryPoint on a standby and in crash recovery, and have the invalid-page failures from v13 and v14 been traced to a cause?

critic.reasoning: The assert failure in message #43 and the untraced invalid-page warnings in messages #27 and #30 are open. The production-build part is overstated, because master also only warns in that case.

objections.title: Spread checkpoints no longer follow checkpoint_completion_target
objections.failure_scenario: A DBA sets checkpoint_completion_target = 0.9 to spread checkpoint writes over the interval. After upgrade, the write phase finishes in about a quarter of the expected time, so the I/O lands in a burst. The DBA sees foreground latency spikes at each checkpoint and has no setting to restore the old pacing.
objections.argument: CheckpointWriteDelay() is now called once per combined write and still sleeps at most 100 ms per call. In message #42 a 26.9 s write phase drops to 7.1 s, and message #43 reports 26.3 s dropping to 11.2 s. The documented meaning of checkpoint_completion_target changes for everyone who uses spread checkpoints, the default case, while the measured gains in message #33 come from immediate checkpoints and backend writes. Message #43 attaches a fix, but v16 has not adopted one.
objections.author_must_show: With combining on, does a spread checkpoint keep the write-phase duration that checkpoint_completion_target asks for, on the setups in messages #42 and #43?

critic.reasoning: Messages #42 and #43 each measure the shorter write phase, and v16 has not adopted a fix. One detail is wrong: message #42 shows io_combine_limit = 8kB restores the old pacing, so a setting does exist.

objections.title: bgwriter_lru_maxpages stops being a hard per-round write limit
objections.failure_scenario: An operator lowers bgwriter_lru_maxpages to cap background writes on shared or IOPS-limited storage. After upgrade, each round can write a whole combined run of up to io_combine_limit blocks, so the bgwriter exceeds the cap. The operator only finds out from pg_stat_io or storage throttling.
objections.argument: Message #42 shows that one call to run_bgwriter_cleaner(1) writes six contiguous buffers, and asks for the remaining budget to be passed into GatherContiguousDirtyBuffers(). Message #43 shows a second effect: neighbors use up the budget, so clock-hand cleaning in 60 s fell from 28000 to 20218 buffers. The proposal does not yet say whether the documented limit counts buffers or IOs. It also does not say whether neighbor writes count against it.
objections.author_must_show: Will bgwriter_lru_maxpages stay a strict per-round buffer limit, and if not, what wording and release note replace its documented meaning?

critic.reasoning: Message #42 shows one cleaner round writing six buffers past the limit, and message #43 shows fewer clock-hand buffers cleaned. The thread has no reply yet on how neighbors count against bgwriter_lru_maxpages.

objections.title: No separate control for foreground neighbor writes
objections.failure_scenario: A latency-sensitive OLTP site keeps a hot set resident and continuously redirtied while VACUUM cycles colder blocks. Each backend that needs a clean buffer also writes up to io_combine_limit of hot neighbors that are dirtied again soon. To stop this, the DBA can only lower io_combine_limit, which also shrinks read combining for sequential scans.
objections.argument: Message #41 describes this adverse case and has no answer yet. Message #37 removed eager_clean_max_batch_size, and message #39 confirms io_combine_limit now caps both reads and writes. The benchmarks in message #33 cover IOPS-limited storage, and message #40 covers WAL-flush cost on local NVMe. Neither measures redundant foreground writes of hot pages, so every backend carries the extra work and no setting turns it off without also losing read combining.
objections.author_must_show: How much write amplification does the hot-set-plus-VACUUM workload from message #41 show, and how would a DBA limit backend neighbor writes without changing read combining?

critic.reasoning: Message #41 describes the hot-set case and the visible thread has no measurement of it; the pgbench runs in message #33 do not model a resident hot set. The request for a measurement stands even if a separate setting is not the right fix.

refuted.title: Renamed dtrace probe silently breaks existing tracing scripts
refuted.failure_scenario: A site traces checkpoint progress with a bpftrace or SystemTap script on buffer__sync__written, keyed by buffer ID. After upgrade the probe is gone and buffers__sync__written reports a count per combined write. The script either fails to attach or gives wrong per-buffer totals, and the user finds out only when the dashboards go blank.
refuted.argument: Message #43 notes that monitoring.sgml still documents the old probe name in 0004. The probes are a documented monitoring interface. v16 renames the probe and changes what its argument means, but the commit message does not mention a release note or migration path. Renaming is safer than changing the meaning under the old name, but users still need the change documented together with 0004.
refuted.author_must_show: Will 0004 update the documented probe table and add a release note telling users how the probe's name and argument changed?

critic.reasoning: The commit message for 0004 states the rename and gives the reason for the new argument. What remains is a monitoring.sgml update, already raised in message #43, and a release note; both are documentation work outside levels 1-2 and apply to any user-visible change.

refuted.title: Buffer-counted limits silently change meaning under combined writes
refuted.failure_scenario: A DBA sets checkpoint_completion_target = 0.9 and bgwriter_lru_maxpages to smooth I/O. After upgrade, spread checkpoints finish in about a quarter of the planned time, and bgwriter rounds write more pages than the limit allows. Nothing logs this. The DBA finds out from I/O latency spikes during checkpoints.
refuted.argument: The series changes the unit of work in checkpointer, bgwriter and backends from one buffer to one combined IO. Existing pacing and limits still count buffers or calls. Two such mismatches stayed unnoticed until reviewers measured them: spread checkpoint pacing (message #42, #43, about 27 s down to 7-11 s) and bgwriter_lru_maxpages being exceeded (message #42, #43). No test or assert fails when a limit and the IO unit drift apart, so later patches that add a write path or a write limit can repeat this.
refuted.author_must_show: Which write-path settings count buffers versus IOs after this series, and what check would catch a future path that ignores one of them?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1 and standards-compat-2, which cover the same two measured mismatches. The added point about future write paths names no concrete case.

touch_points.reason: see objection replication-ondisk-1: Batch checksum on shared lock can write pages with stale checksums

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby

touch_points.label: new GUC

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

committability.owner_note: The panel notes that the author is an active committer in the buffer manager area. The owner must also know recovery, minRecoveryPoint handling and data checksums.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the WAL-before-data rule and checksum correctness on every data write path, in normal running and in recovery, with no end date. The owner also signs for changed pacing of spread checkpoints and bgwriter rounds on existing installations.
committability.author_follow_up: Strong sign. The series reached v16 over about 14 months, and the author posted rebases and revisions in response to reviews.

priority.reason: Message #33 reports about 30% more TPS on IOPS-limited storage, and direct IO needs combined writes, so the gain is broad. The series rewrites core write paths in bufmgr.c and the checkpointer, and four reviewer-measured design points are still open in v16.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so the v16 checksum path, the LSN handling of neighbor blocks in recovery and the cost of the neighbor search on the backend path could not be checked. Only 3 of 43 messages were visible; later messages are known through the objections.

precedents_retrieved.title: Move libpq's write_failed mechanism down to pqsecure_raw_write().
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Move libpq's write_failed mechanism down to pqsecure_raw_write().
Reverted commit(s): Restructure libpq's handling of send failures.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Commit 1f39a1c06 implemented write-failure postponement in pqSendSome,
which is above SSL/GSS processing.  However, we've now seen failures
indicating that (some versions of?) OpenSSL have a tendency to report
write failures prematurely too.  Hence, move the primary responsibility
for postponing write failures down to pqsecure_raw_write(), below
SSL/GSS processing.  pqSendSome now sets write_failed only in corner
cases where we'd lost the connection already.

A side-effect of this change is that errors detected in the SSL/GSS
layer itself will be reported immediately (as if they were read
errors) rather than being postponed like write errors.  That's
reverting an effect of 1f39a1c06, and I think it's fine: if there's
not a socket-level error, it's hard to be sure whether an OpenSSL
error ought to be considered a read or write failure anyway.

Another important point is that write-failure postponement is now
effective during connection setup.  OpenSSL's misbehavior of this
sort occurs during SSL_connect(), so that's a change we want.

Per bug #17391 from Nazir Bilal Yavuz.  Possibly this should be
back-patched, but I think it prudent to let it age awhile in HEAD
first.

precedents_retrieved.title: bloom filter in hash joins with batching
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch builds a bloom filter on the 32-bit hash values of the whole inner relation when a hash join uses batching. Outer tuples with no possible match are then discarded (inner join) or emitted at once (outer join) instead of being written to and read back from batch temp files.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Alvaro Herrera returned it with feedback because even the last version was still at research stage. The author listed open gaps: the filter was not counted in work_mem, outer joins probably did not work, and there was no selectivity-based rule for turning the filter on or off. Peter Geoghegan also pointed to unsolved worst cases, such as high selectivity and skewed outer data.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I'm closing this as returned-with-feedback; AFAICS even the last version submitted is still in research stage.

precedents_retrieved.title: Batch processing of RI checks
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch keeps RI triggers as row-level triggers but passes all queued events of the same kind to the trigger function in one call, so one check query covers many rows. A later version keeps the existing simple queries when only one row needs checking.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier returned the entry because it had been waiting on author for weeks after Andres Freund's June review. That review found the main patch too large, with too little explanation of the new design, and objected to the new infrastructure it adds to trigger.c, including a third copy of the tuples. Earlier, the slower single-row checks and the need for FOR KEY SHARE row locking cast doubt on how much a planned bulk check gains.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I'm pretty unhappy about the amount of new infrastructure this adds to trigger.c.

precedents_retrieved.title: Report checkpoint progress with pg_stat_progress_checkpoint
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Michael Paquier, Andres Freund, Julien Rouhaud
precedents_retrieved.summary: The thread started as a proposal to log checkpoint progress in the server log. After objections it became a pg_stat_progress_checkpoint view that reports the checkpoint phase, flags, start LSN, start time and per-phase counters.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The final close came because the author stopped responding after Andres Freund marked the patch waiting on author for a docs build failure and noted that the architectural feedback had not reached a conclusion. Earlier, Michael Paquier returned it because the view was too complex and carried fields of little use, such as next_flags, start LSN and most flag values. Julien Rouhaud objected that the view showed the initial checkpoint flags instead of how the checkpoint was behaving now. Andres Freund measured progress-update overhead in BufferSync() on large shared_buffers.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: There has been no updates on this thread for some time, so this has been switched as Returned with Feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: hashjoin - gracefully increasing NTUP_PER_BUCKET instead of batching
precedents_retrieved.summary: When the hash table for a hash join does not fit in work_mem at the initial NTUP_PER_BUCKET load factor of 1, the patch tries load factors of 2, 4 and 8 before falling back to batching. If batching becomes necessary at run time, it switches back to the default load factor, and explain shows the load factor.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author's own tests showed that even a load factor of 2 was slower than going to two batches when temp files stay in the page cache; only an outer table large enough to cause real I/O favoured the higher load factor. Kevin Grittner could not build a case where the change won and judged that detecting the cases where it would help would be hard and add cost to every hash join. No one found a reliable way to detect those cases, so the author asked to mark it rejected.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The patch was meant as an attempt to implement Robert's idea
from the hashjoin patch, but apparently we have no clear idea how to do
it without hurting performance for many existing users.

precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a pg_stat_progress_checkpoint view that reports the phase, flags, start LSN and other details of the running checkpoint or restartpoint. It started as a proposal to log checkpoint progress in the server log, but reviewers asked for a progress view instead.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier marked the entry Returned with Feedback because the view needed simplification: several fields and flags were of little use for monitoring, and the phase names were too long. Andres Freund objected that the view definition makes pg_rewrite bigger, and he asked for proof that the progress counters do not slow down checkpoints with many dirty buffers. The last measurement shown, a manual checkpoint taking 2.457 s with the patch against 2.334 s without, got no reply.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I think that what's proposed could be simplified, and we had better remove the fields that are not that useful.

roaster_notes.note: The only close precedent, P2, was set aside in favour of a broader design that would also cover the main writeback paths. This proposal is that broader scope, so the P2 reason does not count against it. P7 is about checkpoint pacing under full_page_writes and has no recorded reason, so it is not used here. The open problems in the thread, such as spread checkpoint pacing (messages #42, #43) and bgwriter_lru_maxpages, are new design issues for other angles.
No SQL syntax, catalog or pg_dump changes are proposed. The objections cover changed meaning of existing settings and of a documented probe.
There is no on-disk format, catalog, WAL record or protocol change, so pg_upgrade and mixed-version replication are not affected. Both objections concern write-path invariants only.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. It changes how the checkpointer, bgwriter and backends write dirty shared buffers. It adds no SQL-callable function, privilege, role or GUC, and no new monitoring output beyond larger pg_stat_io write counts. The test_aio functions that dirty, flush and invalidate blocks are in a test module, not an installed extension. Data-integrity risks such as the hint-bit checksum race, the recovery assert and the invalid-page warning belong to the safety angle, not this one.
Not applicable. Fit and ownership look sound: an active committer in the bufmgr area wrote the series, several reviewers are engaged, and the preparatory patches can be committed on their own.

No existing feature, setting or extension does this job. The *_flush_after settings only send writeback hints for writes already issued one block at a time, and kernel merging does not apply under direct IO. The proposal extends io_combine_limit, the existing read-combining limit, so it adds no second mechanism, and buffer manager internals cannot be replaced from an extension.

Demand is shown in the material. Write throughput on IOPS-limited storage is a broad, common problem, and the author reports about 30% more TPS and 75% better p99 latency in pgbench (message #33). Independent testers saw faster checkpoints (messages #3, #28), and direct IO, a project-wide goal, needs combined writes. The benefit goes to all write-heavy users. The open costs (spread checkpoint pacing, bgwriter_lru_maxpages) are design questions for other angles.
